svg.title: Convert One Cohort Without Counting It Twice
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-qualified-account-cohort; chart type: funnel; title: Convert One Cohort Without Counting It Twice; subtitle: A nested account funnel separates selling activity from earned revenue.; chapter number: 6; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Illustrative single cohort of 200 distinct accounts observed over 120 days; each account appears at most once per stage. Counts are planning assumptions rather than observed conversion benchmarks or annual scorecard inputs.; caption: Sequential conversion is 25%, 40%, 50%, and 40%; overall conversion is 2%. Four accepted $12,500 implementations produce $50,000 of implementation revenue under the stated acceptance assumption; retainers are excluded.; stages: label: Selected accounts; value: 200 accounts with one documented workflow hypothesis; numeric value: 200.0; detail: Build a deduplicated CRM cohort with an identifiable operations owner, a recurring workflow, and a plausible budget. A contact list alone is not evidence of buyer intent.; label: Engaged accounts; value: 50 accounts enter a two-way workflow conversation; numeric value: 50.0; detail: Count substantive replies or booked conversations, not email opens. Fifty divided by 200 gives 25% engagement for the original account cohort.; label: Qualified discoveries; value: 20 accounts verify ownership, budget, and accessible inputs; numeric value: 20.0; detail: Confirm who can authorize system access and accept delivery. Twenty divided by 50 gives 40% qualification; accounts without a bounded use case exit the funnel.; label: Scoped proposals; value: 10 accounts receive priced, testable implementation offers; numeric value: 10.0; detail: Send a fixed-scope statement of work with exclusions, client dependencies, acceptance fixtures, and support options. Ten divided by 20 gives 50% proposal conversion.; label: Accepted implementations; value: 4 accounts complete a $12,500 implementation each; numeric value: 4.0; detail: These four accounts are a subset of the ten proposals. Four divided by ten gives 40% completion conversion. A deposit alone does not establish earned revenue; apply the engagement's recognition policy.

text.title: Convert One Cohort Without Counting It Twice
text.tspan: Convert One Cohort Without Counting It Twice

circle.title: label: Selected accounts; value: 200 accounts with one documented workflow hypothesis; numeric value: 200.0; detail: Build a deduplicated CRM cohort with an identifiable operations owner, a recurring workflow, and a plausible budget. A contact list alone is not evidence of buyer intent.

label: Engaged accounts; value: 50 accounts enter a two-way workflow conversation; numeric value: 50.0; detail: Count substantive replies or booked conversations, not email opens. Fifty divided by 200 gives 25% engagement for the original account cohort.

label: Qualified discoveries; value: 20 accounts verify ownership, budget, and accessible inputs; numeric value: 20.0; detail: Confirm who can authorize system access and accept delivery. Twenty divided by 50 gives 40% qualification; accounts without a bounded use case exit the funnel.

label: Scoped proposals; value: 10 accounts receive priced, testable implementation offers; numeric value: 10.0; detail: Send a fixed-scope statement of work with exclusions, client dependencies, acceptance fixtures, and support options. Ten divided by 20 gives 50% proposal conversion.

label: Accepted implementations; value: 4 accounts complete a $12,500 implementation each; numeric value: 4.0; detail: These four accounts are a subset of the ten proposals. Four divided by ten gives 40% completion conversion. A deposit alone does not establish earned revenue; apply the engagement's recognition policy.

text.title: Assumptions: Illustrative single cohort of 200 distinct accounts observed over 120 days; each account appears at most once per stage. Counts are planning assumptions rather than observed conversion benchmarks or annual scorecard inputs.
